<reason>The motion demanded a comparison of magnitudes, and only B consistently did that work. B's arithmetic showed a ~70% cost collapse even granting CON's worst-case escalation rate, then stress-tested it (triple cost, double failures, still 40%+). A's counters were real but never closed the gap: governance costs were asserted to "erase" savings without any magnitude, liability was countered by the patch-once-fix-everywhere and detection-at-scale points, and A's strongest late card — silent churn invisible to contact ledgers — was neutralized in B's closing as baseline-blind (hold-queue churn exists in the human system too, minus transcripts). A explicitly refused to name any flip threshold, which was reasoned but left B's discounted-arithmetic route intact. A's correlated/fat-tailed risk frame was the debate's best single idea and rhetorically superb, but unquantified exposure can't outweigh measured savings on this motion as written. Both sides complied with Q1/Q2 and A1/A2 formats; neither used fake sourcing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Rebuttal 1 arithmetic (100-contact ledger showing 70%+ savings on CON's own 25% escalation assumption) paired with the repeated flip-rate challenge A never answered with any threshold — and B's closing point that silent churn afflicts the human baseline as well, which A left entirely unanswered.</best_rebuttal>
